text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The Finance Ministry said it would issue a 3-5 billion crown tranche of crown-denominated bonds on foreign markets in the fourth quarter to help cover the budget deficit.
- The ministry also said it planned an unspecified tax on yields from state securities, expected to take effect in the fourth quarter.

- Parliamentary Chairman Ivan Gasparovic has rejected a Constitutional Court ruling that parliament violated the constitution last December when it voted to withdraw the mandate of former ruling coalition deputy Jozef Gaulieder.
- Slovnaft proccessed 2.56 million tonnes of crude oil in the first six months of the year, around half of the amount the company plans to proccess in 1997.

- The government on Tuesday approved a long-term framework strategy for financing motorway construction. The strategy foresees two alternatives -- one with state budget coverage of 50 percent of expenditures and the remaining half covered by loans, while the second alternative sees the entire sum needed for highway construction to be covered by loans.

- Leading packaging materials producer AssiDoman Packaging Sturovo a.s. said it planned to invest some 225 million crowns in 1997. The company also said it planned investment projects worth 1.5 billion crowns in the next few years.
SME - Three main parties representing the Hungarian minority in Slovakia have agreed to create a coalition before the next parliamenatry election scheduled for autumn 1998.
- Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar and his Hungarian counterpoart Gyula Horn are expected to discuss bilateral relations and integration to Western structures during their meeting on Friday.
PRAVDA - Overall car imports to Slovakia totalled 8.2 billion crowns in the first half of 1997, down from 9.3 billion in the same period last year.

- Auto exports rose to 7.7 billion crowns in the January-June period of 1997, up from last year's 2.0 bilion crowns. Car exports were boosted mainly by production at Volkswagen's Bratislava assembly plant.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The state-owned postal monopoly Slovenska Posta posted a profit of 595 million crowns in the first half of 1997 on revenues totaling 1.05 billion crowns.
